title: 62:4 Forsaken/Desolate/Delightful/Union. Because the image of this passage is that of marriage, these adjectives represent the contrast between Israel in her exiled state and as the covenant wife (which is latter-day Zion) of Jehovah. Before her deliverance and redemption, she was seen as forsaken, abandoned by her husband, and desolate—deserted, barren, and without hope. But all that will be forgotten in her glorious future (54:1, 6-8; 60:14-15). Then she will be known as Hephzi-bah ("My delight is in her," or "Delightful") and Beulah ("married wife" or "Union").
author: Tina M. Peterson
